newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds were drifting to a moderately stronger finish Wednesday, having largely ignored an earlier investment grade BBB- rating of the country by Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co.
The government's R150 bond was last traded at 14.645 percent from Tuesday's 1400 GMT level of 14.660 percent.
"There was a little bit of demand after the Duff & Phelps rating but that's dissappeared. It's been fairly quiet all day," said a Johannesburg-based bond dealer.
"If it goes through 14.58 with some conviction tonight then it could go a lot better but, really, the momentum's just not there ahead of July 1."
On July 1, South African individuals will be allowed to invest offshore for the first time, a move that has prompted fears among some market participants of an exodus of capital from the country.

The R150 opened in the red as players brushed off Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's upbeat overnight interest rate outlook as adding little to last week's comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals.
Jobbers sold the benchmark yield to it's session worst of 14.70 percent before being surprised by fresh demand.

The ensuing scramble and a sizeable order of R153s drove the R150 to 14.605 before the rating news, of which there had been scattered murmurs beforehand. The rating excitement quickly dissipated, however.
"It was nice to see the rating but I think something from S&P (Standard & Poor's) would have held my attention longer," noted one dealer.
The South African rand looked healthier but rangebound in late dealings as carry trades and a good supply of dollars overall kept the mood buoyant.
The rand was last changing hands at 4.4960/4990 from Tuesday's late price of 4.5010/5040.

"There was a bunch of dollars out there. I think a few people were long after the rand's slide on Monday and a little profit taking came in during the morning plus the carries helped us out," said one forex dealer.
But he added unwinding of carry trades early Thursday might see the rand testing 4.50 once more.
The rand did little to shake off its early weakness against the yen, clocking up a fresh five-month low at 24.6665/6941 from 24.9906/0206 late Tuesday.
Against the mark and pound, however, the rand improved. It was last quoted at 0.3812/3816 marks from 0.3807/3810 marks Tuesday and 7.3556/3626 on sterling from 7.3783/3877 previously.
South Africa's money market shortage was broadly unchanged on Tuesday, coming in at 7.12 billion rand from 7.190 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates lined up at 16.05 percent offered, unchanged from Tuesday, while the 90-day BA rate remained pegged at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent.
Foreigners were net buyers of 540.92 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 346.63 million rand's worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes slipped to 4.99 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.29 billion rand on Monday.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
